faq.q: Is June a good month for a Marbella boat rental?
faq.a: Yes — June offers warm sea temperatures (21–28°C), long sunny days, and lighter crowds than July or August. The Levante wind can pick up in the afternoon, but mornings are typically calm. It's an excellent month for coastal cruising, snorkelling, and anchoring in coves like Cala del Faro.

faq.q: What is the weather like in Marbella in June 2027?
faq.a: Expect average highs of 28–30°C, sea temperatures around 21–23°C early month, rising to 26–28°C by late June. Winds are typically 10–15 knots from the east (Levante), with occasional stronger gusts. Rainfall is rare — usually 0–2 days. UV index is high, so bring sunscreen.

faq.q: Which boat is best for June conditions?
faq.a: For calm mornings, any boat works well. If Levante winds pick up, larger vessels like the Mangusta 80 (24m) or Ferretti 94 (29m) offer more stability. The Azimut 58 Flybridge (17.6m) gives you a sheltered flybridge for windy afternoons. For smaller groups, the Speedboat (7m) is fine in light winds.

faq.q: How far in advance should I book a boat in June?
faq.a: We recommend booking 2–3 weeks ahead for weekdays and at least 4 weeks for weekends. June is popular for corporate events and stag/hen groups, so availability tightens quickly. Contact us via WhatsApp for real-time availability.

faq.q: What is included in the charter price?
faq.a: Every charter includes a licensed skipper, fuel, water, soft drinks, beer, white wine, cava, light snacks, insurance, safety equipment, and Spanish IVA (21%). No hidden fees. See our fleet page for full details.

faq.q: Can I bring my own food and drinks?
faq.a: Yes, you're welcome to bring your own food and additional drinks. Our standard provision includes soft drinks, beer, and cava. If you want a catered menu, let us know in advance and we can arrange it at an extra cost.

faq.q: What happens if the weather is bad on my booked day?
faq.a: We monitor forecasts closely. If conditions are unsafe (e.g., strong Levante winds over 25 knots or thunderstorms), we'll offer a free reschedule or full refund. Our skippers have the final say on safety. June rarely causes cancellations.

faq.q: Are there any hidden costs for fuel or mooring?
faq.a: No — fuel is included in the charter price. Mooring fees at Puerto Banús and any stops we make (e.g., Cabopino, Estepona) are covered. You only pay for extras like jet skis, water toys, or premium catering if requested.

Whether you're planning a family day out, a corporate event, or a celebration, this guide gives you the numbers, the advice, and the boat options to make it happen from Puerto Banús.

We operate a fleet of 16 boats from Puerto Banús, Marbella's most famous marina. All charters include a licensed skipper, fuel, drinks, snacks, and insurance. No surprises. Here's what you need to know.

June Weather in Marbella: The Numbers

June marks the start of high season on the Costa del Sol. Average air temperatures hover around 28–30°C, with sea temperatures climbing from 21°C early in the month to 28°C by the end. That's warm enough for swimming without a wetsuit.

  • Daylight: 14.5 hours — sunrise ~07:00, sunset ~21:30.
  • Wind: 10–15 knots typical, with occasional Levante gusts up to 30 knots in the afternoon.
  • Rain: 0–2 rainy days on average. UV index: 9+ — bring factor 50.
  • Sea state: Calm in the morning; moderate chop possible after 14:00 if Levante blows.

Best Boats for June Conditions

For calm mornings, any boat works. But if the Levante picks up, size matters. Here's a quick guide based on our fleet:

Tier A boats (Astondoa 40, Azimut 39) start at €749 for 2 hours, all inclusive. Tier B (Mangusta 80) from €4,719 for 4 hours, with a free jet ski. All other boats — pricing on request via WhatsApp.

Where to Cruise in June

With long daylight, you can cover more ground. Popular routes from Puerto Banús include:

  • West to Estepona: 12 NM, 45 minutes. Anchor at Playa del Cristo or the marina.
  • East to Cabopino: 8 NM, 30 minutes. Quiet coves and the Artola dunes.
  • South to Cala del Faro: 5 NM, 20 minutes. Snorkelling and cliff jumping.
  • Full day to Sotogrande: 25 NM, 1.5 hours. Luxury marina and lunch at La Alcaidesa.

If the Levante blows, stick to the western side of the bay — Estepona and Sotogrande are more sheltered.

Booking Advice for June 2027

June is popular, especially for weekends and corporate charters. We recommend booking at least 2–3 weeks ahead for weekdays, 4 weeks for weekends. Contact us via WhatsApp for real-time availability.

All charters include skipper, fuel, drinks, snacks, insurance, and IVA. No hidden costs. You can bring your own food. If weather turns bad, we offer free rescheduling or a full refund — our skippers have the final say on safety.

What to Pack for a June Charter

  • Sunscreen (SPF 50+, water-resistant)
  • Hat and sunglasses
  • Swimwear and a towel
  • Light jacket or windbreaker (for afternoon breeze)
  • Camera or phone for photos

The Marbella boat rental weather June 2027 is ideal — just be ready for a possible afternoon wind. Plan your morning departure, and you'll have calm seas and warm water.
